english.title: Use undue influence at election by threatening violence, force, restraint, injury, damage, harm or loss
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of undue influence and therefore a corrupt practice in that you directly or indirectly, by yourself or by another person on your behalf,

(A)_[made use of or threatened to make use of force, violence or restraint]_
(B)_[inflicted or threatened to inflict, by yourself or by another person, temporal or spiritual injury, damage, harm or loss]_

upon or against a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),

(C)_[in order to induce or compel that person to vote or refrain from voting]_
(D)_[on account of that person having voted or refrained from voting]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 115(1) and (2)(a) and 168(1) of the Representation of the People Act 1983

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
